title: Predictive soft-cap crediting model and billing acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: Large customers have variable traffic with irregular spikes that often trigger immediate overage charges or manual refunds. Current gracebanding and manual credits create operational overhead and inconsistent customer experience. We want a predictive soft-cap model that awards temporary soft credits proactively when usage patterns indicate an imminent exceedance, smoothing invoices and reducing manual reconciliation. This ticket defines product requirements and acceptance criteria for the pilot implementation and initial billing correctness checks.
requirements: Design a predictive engine surface that consumes historical per-tenant hourly usage (last 30 days) and current-day trend to estimate the likelihood of exceeding monthly entitlements within a 72-hour horizon.

Define a soft-cap credit that applies automatically up to a configurable percentage of a plan's monthly quota (default 10%) and that is visible on the tenant billing UI and invoices as 'temporary soft-credit'.

Credits granted by the predictive model must be time-bound (expiry timestamp) and automatically reconciled at month-end: either convert to permanent credit, be billed, or offset by future usage according to reconciliation rules.
Admin controls: allow account-level toggles (on/off), adjustable soft-cap percentage, and audit logs for when credits were applied/removed and by which mechanism (predictive vs manual).
Ensure billing ledger entries are immutable once committed; prior to commit, soft-credit changes appear in a provisional ledger visible to billing ops with a clear state flag.
Expose API and Console endpoints for querying active provisional soft-credits, reasoning score (likelihood), and the model version that issued the credit for future auditability.
Operational constraints: predictive decisions must complete within 200ms for tenant evaluation path; bulk nightly reconciliation jobs may run asynchronously with idempotency guarantees.
Fallback: if predictive system is unavailable, system must default to current graceband behavior (no automated soft-credits) and raise an alert to ops.
Provide a read-only dataset export for finance containing soft-credit events, tenant IDs, amounts, reason codes, and final reconciliation outcome for audit purposes.
Privacy/security: ensure exported datasets and API surfaces respect PII minimization and KMS encryption of exported files.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive evaluation returns a clear decision for 95% of tenants with non-zero usage within 72 hours in production-like load tests.

When predictive soft-credit is applied, the tenant invoice preview in Console shows the provisional soft-credit line item and an explanatory tooltip, matching ledger preview within 1 cent in all tested currencies.

All provisional soft-credit events are recorded in the provisional ledger with state values: CREATED, CONFIRMED, RECONCILED, or EXPIRED. Transition rules behave deterministically in reconciliation tests.

Monthly reconciliation job produces deterministic outcomes given fixed seed data in staging and matches acceptance test expectations for convert/bill/offset paths in >= 99% of cases in end-to-end tests.
Audit API returns the credit event history and model version for any tenant ID for the last 12 months within 3 seconds for typical queries (<= 100 events).
System falls back to existing graceband behavior with no soft-credit when predictive infra is deliberately disabled; this is validated in the feature-flagged test node.
Finance receives an export with required fields and a schema agreement file; a sample export for 1,000 events imports cleanly into the finance team's ingestion pipeline without transformation errors.
Latency: live predictive evaluation path for a single tenant completes within 200ms (p95) during synthetic load tests that replicate average cluster utilization.
Security: exported files are encrypted with KMS and access controls enforced; security review signs off on export flow in staging environment.
Documentation: Console copy, API docs, and billing FAQ are drafted and reviewed by Finance and Legal before feature launch.
metrics: % reduction in manual crediting incidents reported by billing ops (target: 60% reduction in pilot accounts)
false positive rate where soft-credit is applied but later fully billed back (target < 8%)
time-to-decision for predictive evaluation (p95 in ms)
proportion of tenants covered by predictive model with sufficient historical data (target > 85%)
reconciliation mismatch rate between provisional ledger and final invoice (target < 0.5%)
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: Implement predictive evaluation service in staging with synthetic tenants and feature flag gating.
Week 3: Integrate provisional ledger entries, console preview, and API surfaces; run closed QA with finance team using snapshot data.
Week 4: Start a controlled pilot on 10 low-risk enterprise customers (opt-in) and monitor metrics daily; bill normally but provide internal finance offsets for pilot discrepancies.
Week 6: Expand pilot to 100 accounts if pilot KPIs meet thresholds; run reconciliation automation and perform a security review.
Week 8: If pilot success criteria met, schedule full launch with marketing and support playbooks; otherwise roll back automated granting and proceed to root-cause analysis.
Feature flag controls and a manual override button for billing ops are included throughout rollout.
Post-launch: 30/60/90 day reviews with finance, ops, and product to tune thresholds and model behaviour.
risks: Model over-crediting increases short-term revenue leakage if reconciliation criteria are off; mitigate with conservative default cap and finance buffer.
Complexity of ledger states increases billing pipeline risk; require thorough end-to-end tests and canary on staging pipeline before prod reconciliation runs.
Customer confusion if UI messaging is unclear; include tooltip and email communication templates to pilot customers.
Regulatory/audit scrutiny on automated crediting; ensure exportability and immutable records for auditors.
Operational load: real-time prediction per-tenant could strain serving clusters during spikes; implement rate-limiting and graceful degradation path.
